title: feat(types): re-export BreadcrumbSchema and ObjectTreeSchema from the zod barrel (objectui#7917)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectui#7917

## What changed

`packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts` now re-exports two names whose modules already declared them:

- `BreadcrumbSchema` from `./navigation.zod.js`
- `ObjectTreeSchema` from `./objectql.zod.js`

Both were already `export const` in their own module. What was missing was the barrel — and `index.zod.ts` is the package's only zod entry point, which `base.zod.ts` states in as many words on `defineNodeComponentUnion`: "the package's only zod entry point is the `./zod` barrel, which is `index.zod.ts`". Plus a pin test and a `minor` changeset. No schema, no accept set and no union membership moved.

## The reading, re-taken on current main

The card measured 107 / 105 / 2 at `fa7d66c4`. Two things made that worth re-taking rather than inheriting: `origin/main` has moved a great deal (`ObjectTreeSchema` sits at `objectql.zod.ts` line 870 now, not 742), and comment 5563937304 showed the original probe resolved union arms through a handle that under-reports — `S.unwrap()` and `S._zod.def.getter()` both read around zod 4.4.3's `_cachedInner`, which is why the objectui#7581 measurement called `ActionSchema` unexported when it plainly is.

Re-taken with `_zod.innerType`, against `packages/types/dist/zod/index.zod.js` built from the tree under test:

| commit | arms declared | with a named export | without |
|---|---|---|---|
| `efbd566d2` (branch point) | 107 | 105 | 2 — `breadcrumb`, `object-tree` |
| `a5eaf49c3` (this PR, merged head) | 107 | 107 | 0 |

Controls in the same run on the same handle: `TreeViewSchema`, `TreeNodeSchema`, `PaginationSchema` and `ObjectGanttSchema` all resolve, and so does `ActionSchema` — so the handle is the stable one and the two zeros are a reading rather than a repeat of the old false negative. Also measured: 107 distinct `type` literals, zero collisions.

## Establishing intent first — the card refused to assume the repair

The card is explicit that it does not claim every node schema must be individually exported, and that there may be a deliberate reason these two are internal. So the repair was taken only after looking for that reason, with a live control so that "found nothing" is a reading rather than a search that missed.

**The control: this directory does record deliberate non-export, in as many words, when it holds.** Three markers, all inside `packages/types/src/zod/`:

- `base.zod.ts` on `defineNodeComponentUnion` — "`@internal` ... this exists for that one call site and is not re-exported."
- `complex.zod.ts` on `ChatbotSharedMirrorShape` — "Not exported: it is a census, not a mirror ..."
- `objectql.zod.ts` on `GanttConfigExtensionFields` — "Not exported: the parity census ... reads `^export const` out of this directory and would require a registered TS counterpart" — in the very file `ObjectTreeSchema` lives in.

Against that control, what the two arms carry is nothing: both docblocks are bare one-liners ("Breadcrumb Schema - Breadcrumb navigation", "ObjectTree (tree-grid) Schema").

Everything else checked, and what it said:

- **Barrel comment** — the `./navigation.zod.js` and `./objectql.zod.js` export blocks list every sibling arm with no omission note. Navigation carried 5 of its 6 arms, objectql 11 of its 12.
- **Ledger row** — the parity census registers both as first-class mirrors with a registered TS counterpart (`navigation.zod.ts#BreadcrumbSchema`, `objectql.zod.ts#ObjectTreeSchema`) rather than exempting them, and it imports them by module path, so it is unaffected either way.
- **A prior ruling on the card** — triage comment 5557229847 lays out option (a) add the exports and option (b) rule them deliberately internal plus a gate, and says in terms that this is an observation, not a ruling. Comment 5563937304 is about probe method only. Neither rules them internal.
- **ADR** — nothing in `docs/adr/` touches the export surface.
- **A gate that would refuse it** — the only script reading `index.zod` is `scripts/measure-strict-authoring-face.mjs`, which its own header calls a MEASUREMENT THROWAWAY. `check:readme-exports` judges import statements, not bullet lists. No test pins an export-name list or an export count for this barrel, and the repo holds no API snapshot.
- **History** — 471 commits deep after `git fetch --deepen 400`, `git log -S` on the barrel returns zero hits for either symbol, with a live control leg: the same probe for `TreeViewSchema` hits `9587fc959`. Neither name was added and then deliberately removed inside that window.

**One piece of evidence points the other way:** the barrel's own `packages/types/src/zod/README.md` lists `BreadcrumbSchema` twice under "Available Schemas" (Data Display, and Navigation). That README ships in the package tarball, so the barrel documented the name as available and did not deliver it.

Nothing marks the two deliberate, so the invariant "a declared arm is nameable" — which 105 of 107 already held — is restored here, rather than a product question being decided.

## One PM mechanism assumption falsified — the pin asserts what is true, not what was predicted

The dispatch owed a pin whose refusal "names the key rather than an `invalid_union` over 107 arms". **Measured, that half no longer describes main.** Since objectui#8498 made `AnyComponentSchema` a *discriminated* union, it selects one arm from the authored literal and already diagnoses a wrong-typed key by name:

```
BreadcrumbSchema.safeParse({ type:'breadcrumb', items:[{label:'Home'}], maxItems:'five' })
  => [{ code: 'invalid_type', path: ['maxItems'], expected: 'number' }]   message 168 chars
AnyComponentSchema.safeParse(the same document)
  => [{ code: 'invalid_type', path: ['maxItems'], expected: 'number' }]   message 168 chars
```

What survives — and what no union can ever answer — is the **question**, not the message:

```
AnyComponentSchema.safeParse({ type: 'button', label: 'Save' })  => success: true
BreadcrumbSchema.safeParse({ type: 'button', label: 'Save' })    => success: false
```

The union answers "is this SOME valid node". Only the named schema answers "is this a valid breadcrumb", which is what a designer, a form builder or a targeted test needs. So the pin's third leg asserts that asymmetry rather than the message shape the card predicted.

## The pin

`packages/types/src/__tests__/breadcrumb-object-tree-nameable-7917.test.ts`, 9 tests, modelled on `objectql-union-arms-7363.test.ts`, three legs per name:

1. the name resolves off the barrel;
2. it is a real declaration — a minimal document is accepted, and a wrong-typed DECLARED key is refused with the refusal naming that key. `BaseSchema` is passthrough, so an unknown key would prove nothing; both probes are keys the mirror declares (`maxItems`, `defaultExpandedDepth`);
3. the question asymmetry above.

**Reverse verification** — the repair was committed first, the mutation proven on disk by blob hash, and the restore done with `git checkout HEAD -- path` and proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`:

- both re-export lines deleted: HEAD blob `d6fe74c4` against on-disk `4d26387c`, anchored line counts 1/1 to 0/0;
- the pin went RED: `Test Files 1 failed`, `Tests 8 failed | 1 passed`. The single survivor is leg 3's control half — that `AnyComponentSchema` accepts a button — which is precisely the assertion that does not depend on this change;
- restored: on-disk blob back to `d6fe74c4`, `git diff HEAD` empty, pin green again at 9 of 9.

## Gates

Hand-derived from objectui's `package.json` and `.github/workflows/`, since `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` refuses objectui paths. Exit codes captured as `cmd > file 2>&1; EXIT=$?`, never through a pipe, and every verdict read from the gate's own printed line. All re-run on the merged head `a5eaf49c3`.

| command | exit |
|---|---|
| `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/types --force` | 0 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` | 0 — 156 files, 3082 tests passed |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/breadcrumb-object-tree-nameable-7917.test.ts` | 0 — 9 passed |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types lint` | 0 — 0 errors, 266 pre-existing warnings, none in the changed files |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-unreferenced-sources.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` | 0 — NOT GOVERNED, 3 paths against 5 surfaces |
| `node scripts/check-readme-exports.mjs` | 1 — prerequisite not met, see below |
| `node scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs` | 1 — prerequisite not met, see below |

Two reds, neither from this diff, both declared to CI which builds cleanly:

- **`check:readme-exports`** reports 522 "could not be judged ... run `pnpm build` first" lines across 33 packages whose `dist/` this worktree never built. Zero of those lines involve `@object-ui/types`, whose dist IS on disk and whose README was judged. The judgeable half is green: 22 real self-imports, 0 fabricated, 0 wrong-path. That gate can only fail on a name that is imported and missing, so adding exports cannot push it toward red.
- **`check:node-esm-load`** exits 1 on its provenance leg, not its load leg: 35 of 37 gradable entries were built by this tree and 2 were replayed into it out of another worktree's turbo cache (`@object-ui/auth` and `@object-ui/react-runtime`, both from a sibling review worktree; turbo shares one cache across every worktree of a checkout). `@object-ui/types` is in scope and in neither refusal bucket. Worth recording the shape: the shell wrapper around that gate reported "exit code 0" while the gate's own line read `EXIT=1`.

Type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` (no `projectService`, no `project:`, no `parserOptions`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch.

## Contract review, and why this stays a draft

`Clause-②: yes` — two named exports widen the published surface of `@object-ui/types/zod`, so this is built at this tier and reviewed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. It carries `needs:contract-review` and stays a **draft**: not flipped ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge.

## Overlap

`packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts` is also edited by objectui#6910 (branch `claude/issue-6910-retire-event-handlers-schema`), which removes the `EventHandlersSchema` re-export while this adds two — different regions of one barrel. That line is untouched here and still sits at line 83. `origin/main` was merged into this branch at `fb3a10106` with no conflict, and will be merged again if that sibling lands while this is open. Conflicts go to the merge queue; no ordering is arranged by hand.

## Acceptance notes

Noted while working, deliberately not repaired here and not filed:

- **The TypeScript face has the same hole for `ObjectTreeSchema`, and only for it.** `packages/types/src/index.ts` does not re-export `ObjectTreeSchema`, while siblings `ObjectMapSchema` (line 425) and `ObjectGanttSchema` (line 427) are exported and `BreadcrumbSchema` (line 299) is exported. Verified on current `origin/main` with a live control. Comment 5565353690 already records this on the card, and it sits outside this dispatch's declared file surface, so it stays open there rather than becoming a new card.
- **`BreadcrumbItemSchema` is not on the barrel either**, while the sibling item schemas `ButtonGroupButtonSchema` and `NavigationMenuItemSchema` are. It is a sub-schema, not one of the 107 arms, so it is outside what this card measured, and a consumer can use `BreadcrumbSchema` without naming it. Whoever picks up the TypeScript-face half above is the natural carrier.
- **Nothing detects this class.** Per the card's own framing and triage option (b): when arm 108 arrives, the same inconsistency can reappear silently. A gate would shut the whole class rather than these two instances — deliberately not added here, per dispatch, and offered as a follow-up for the PM to weigh against its cost.
